text: Charlotte Lee, Lady Baltimore (born 13 March 1678, (13 March 1678 OS); died 1 February 1721, (22 January 1721 OS)), was an English noblewoman and granddaughter of King Charles II of England and his mistress Barbara Villiers, Countess of Castlemaine, Duchess of Cleveland. She was the eldest of at least fourteen children of Edward Henry Lee, 1st Earl of Lichfield (4 February 1663 – 14 July 1716), and Lady Charlotte Fitzroy (5 September 1664 – 17 February 1718), who was the illegitimate daughter of King Charles II by Barbara Villiers. Her mother was thirteen and her father was fifteen at the time of Charlotte's birth. Her paternal grandparents were Sir Francis Henry Lee of Ditchley, 4th Baronet of Quarendon, and Elizabeth Pope, daughter of Thomas Pope, 2nd Earl of Downe. On 2 January 1699, at the age of twenty, she married Benedict Leonard Calvert, son of Charles Calvert, 3rd Baron Baltimore, and Jane Lowe. In February 1715, she assumed the title of Lady Baltimore after her husband succeeded to the title of 4th Baron Baltimore upon the death of his father, the third Baron. The title of Proprietary Governor of the Province of Maryland had been lost during the Glorious Revolution and would be restored to Charles Calvert, the son of Charlotte and Benedict, upon his death on 16 April 1715. Charlotte and Lord Baltimore had six children, including Charles Calvert, 5th Baron Baltimore, and Benedict Leonard Calvert, who served as Governor of Maryland from 1727 to 1731. The couple separated in 1705; in 1706, Charlotte had an affair with Colonel Robert Fielding, then the bigamous husband of her grandmother the Duchess of Cleveland, and it was rumoured she bore a child by him, born on 23 April 1707. In 1711, Lord Baltimore introduced a Bill before the House of Lords to confirm their divorce, settle their finances, and declare any future children of Charlotte illegitimate. In 1719, before 10 December, she married Christopher Crowe (c.1681 – 9 November 1749), Consul at Leghorn, who was three years younger than her. This marriage produced five additional children. Charlotte Lee died of rheumatism on 22 January 1721 at Woodford Hall, Woodford, Essex, and was buried there on 29 January 1721. She died intestate, and her estate was administered on 4 March 1721 at Woodford Hall. Charlotte Lee is a minor character in Anya Seton's historical romance Devil Water.
